narrative:
The assessment estimated a 41.0% probability that you would be a bad credit risk. Under the lending policy applied to your application, that was above the acceptable risk level, so your loan was denied.

The strongest influence on the decision was your credit history. Your record falls into the critical/other-credits group; although this is not a clean record, this factor actually worked in your favour in the final assessment, helping offset other concerns. The next most important factor was your checking-account status. A balance in the 0–200 DM range pushed the decision toward bad credit; most approved applicants had no checking account (59.2%), and only 18.4% had a 0–200 DM balance. Your savings also increased the risk: savings below 100 DM worked against you, even though this is common among approved applicants (45.6%), because stronger savings would have been more reassuring. Your requested term of 30 months and amount of 5,234 DM are also above the approved averages of about 19 months and 3,020 DM, which likely added pressure.

To improve your chances, ask the lender what specific changes would make your profile acceptable. Focus on building savings above 100 DM, moving your checking balance into a healthier range, and consider requesting a smaller amount or shorter term. You can then provide updated financial information and reapply.
